stories.question: Why did semiconductor and AI-hardware stocks fall broadly on October 30, and is this one AI-capex repricing or separate pressures?

time_basis.current_observation: Observed intraday at 18:35 UTC on 30 October 2026; these are snapshots, not final close prices.

background_events.event: Intel beat third-quarter expectations but guided fourth-quarter revenue below consensus, with management saying memory shortages and PC inventory cuts accelerated.
Alphabet fell about 13% and lost about $482 billion in market value after its Q3 results raised AI-return concerns.
Amazon reported 39% AWS revenue growth but a record trailing-12-month free-cash outflow above $42 billion because of infrastructure spending.

time_basis.report_dates: Benzinga coverages published 2026-10-30; retained research for Intel, Alphabet and Amazon dated 2026-10-29; market observation at 18:35 UTC and briefing as of 18:50 UTC.

stories.event_title: Intel's weak fourth-quarter outlook and separate AI-return worries pressure semiconductor and AI-hardware stocks on October 30
stories.surface_summary_text: The semiconductor selloff is not one company-specific breakdown: Intel's weak PC guidance hit PC and memory names, while AI-return worries after Alphabet and Amazon pressured AI suppliers. High bond yields made the broad de-risking easier.
stories.what_happened_text: Intel beat third-quarter expectations but guided fourth-quarter revenue below consensus. Management said memory shortages and PC inventory cuts accelerated. That report directly hit PC and memory names. At the same time, Alphabet's shares fell sharply and lost about $482 billion in market value after its results raised questions about returns on AI investment, while Amazon showed record cash outflow despite fast AWS growth.
stories.why_happened_text: Management tied the PC reset to memory shortages and PC inventory cuts; Gartner and Counterpoint data support a real volume decline. The AI-return leg is different: investors reprice long-duration AI spending when returns look uncertain and funding costs are high. Broad co-movement is sector de-risking, not proof that every supplier lost orders.
stories.affected_assets_summary_text: Dell and HP fell hardest on the PC link; memory and storage names fell with them. Nvidia, Broadcom, Marvell, TSMC, equipment and optical suppliers fell with the AI-return repricing, but no supplied source ties each one to Alphabet or Amazon.
stories.business_context_text: The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.05% and the real yield 2.67% on October 28. That makes long-duration AI buildouts harder to value and explains shared declines even among companies without direct Intel PC exposure.
stories.watch_next_text: Dell's November 24 earnings or OEM comments on sell-through versus price and inventory; any sign memory prices or supply normalize before the first half of 2027.

stories.question: Why is Reddit down sharply on October 30 despite better-than-expected Q3 earnings, and how far does the Google-search user-growth problem extend?

time_basis.current_observation: At 16:35 UTC on 30 October 2026, RDDT was down about 29.18%; this is an intraday observation, not a final close.

background_events.event: Reddit reported Q3 profit and revenue above expectations but Q4 sales guidance below estimates; revenue growth slowed below its recent run rate; daily active uniques grew 12%, below analyst expectations, and U.S. daily active uniques fell 2%.
CEO Steve Huffman said Google search referral traffic declined meaningfully in Q3 because of Google's AI answers and expects the trend to continue.
A Seeking Alpha note dated August 6 argued Reddit was a sell on a stretched multiple versus decelerating user growth.

time_basis.report_dates: CNBC report 2026-10-29; current price observation 2026-10-30 at 16:35 UTC; Seeking Alpha note 2026-08-06.

stories.event_title: Reddit's Q4 guidance and U.S. daily-user decline, tied to shrinking Google search referrals, drive the stock down even after a Q3 beat
stories.surface_summary_text: The issue is future ad inventory, not current revenue: fewer Google search referrals slow user acquisition, and Reddit is testing login requirements outside the U.S.
stories.what_happened_text: Reddit beat Q3 profit and revenue expectations, but fourth-quarter sales guidance came in below estimates. Revenue growth slowed below the pace of the prior eight quarters. The company said daily active uniques grew 12%, but less than analysts expected, and U.S. daily active uniques fell 2%. CEO Steve Huffman said Google search referral traffic dropped meaningfully because Google shifted to AI answers.
stories.why_happened_text: Most revenue comes from app and logged-in direct users, so the search decline is mainly an audience-acquisition problem that reduces future ad inventory and growth, not an immediate loss of the core direct ad audience. The planned login test is a response: it could turn anonymous visitors into registered users better suited to targeted ads, but some visitors may leave instead.
stories.affected_assets_summary_text: Snap, Pinterest and Meta also fell on October 30, which is consistent with sector caution, but no supplied source establishes that Reddit caused those moves.
stories.business_context_text: An earlier Seeking Alpha note raised the valuation-versus-growth concern. Reddit's other revenue, which includes data licensing, grew 35% to $48 million, and its two largest partners are OpenAI and Google, so the Google relationship also has a paying side.
stories.watch_next_text: The start date and scope of the outside-U.S. login test; whether U.S. daily active uniques fall again in the fourth quarter.
